phases.name: AI routing resilience: native DeepSeek registration, file-access-aware routing, wall-clock degraded-state detection
phases.description:
Operator directive 2026-08-01: accepted the adopted/adopt-modified recommendations from the same-day "AI Workforce Architecture" validation report (uploads/kai-ai-workforce-architecture-review-2026-08-01.md), explicitly rejecting the proposal's org-chart staffing model, 9-model parallel pipeline, 2-key-per-provider credential scheme, and 15-factor routing formula -- none of those are in scope for this phase. Three concrete, verified-grounded improvements only:

(1) FORMALIZE NATIVE DEEPSEEK PROVIDERS: core.llm_clients.call_deepseek_native_pro/call_deepseek_native_flash (added 2026-08-01, direct api.deepseek.com calls using dedicated DEEPSEEK_NATIVE_PRO_API_KEY/DEEPSEEK_NATIVE_FLASH_API_KEY, confirmed live: model IDs deepseek-v4-pro/deepseek-v4-flash, ~1.6s response time) exist only as raw llm_clients functions called directly by a scratch script -- register them properly via core.ai_provider.register_provider(), following the exact pattern every other provider in that file already uses (run_text_task, available_fn checking the two new env vars, cost_tier="free_or_low_cost", kind="cloud"). Add them into core.ai.ai_router.ROLE_PROVIDERS as fallback capacity for text_task roles (planning/documentation/review) -- per 17M's already-established rule, new providers slot in AFTER existing top-priority providers, never ahead of or displacing them.

(2) REQUIRES_FILE_ACCESS ROUTING FLAG: add a requires_file_access: bool parameter to core.ai.ai_router.delegate() (default True, matching todays real behavior where coding-capable calls assume file access). When True, candidate filtering excludes providers with no run_coding_task/tool-use capability (i.e. keeps routing through the OpenCode-CLI-mediated family that can read real files and cite verified line numbers). When False, the native DeepSeek providers from (1) and other plain text_task providers become eligible, trading file-grounding for speed -- this directly addresses tonights confirmed-live finding that a file-blind reviewer measurably produced thinner, less-accurate architecture plans than a file-grounded one for the same roadmap phase (13H), so this flag must default to preserving grounding, not defatt to speed.

(3) WALL-CLOCK TIMEOUT-BASED DEGRADED-STATE DETECTION: extend core.ai.provider_health.py to record a temporary degraded/error snapshot when a provider call exceeds a configurable wall-clock threshold (starting point: 120s, tunable), independent of whether the provider ever returns a clean HTTP 429 -- confirmed live tonight that Claude Fable 5 (opencode_claude) hit repeated 300-550s+ silent wall-clock timeouts with no error response at all, which the existing quota_exceeded/error capture never caught since those require an actual HTTP error to fire on. A demoted provider is deprioritized (not hard-excluded) in candidate ordering for a cooldown window (starting point: 15 minutes), then naturally re-evaluated on its next real usage-history read -- this is deliberately the SAME kind of pre-emptive-degradation gap already scoped into roadmap phase 13L (amended 2026-08-01), so implement this as an amendment/companion to 13Ls provider_health work, not a competing mechanism.

Explicitly out of scope (rejected per the review, do not implement): any per-model dedicated-API-key reservation scheme (the real credential structure -- one shared opencode Zen slot across 4 providers, one shared main OpenRouter key across 4 providers -- makes this structurally impossible without the operator acquiring genuinely new keys, which was not requested here), any multi-factor (15-factor) per-request scoring engine, any org-chart-style named division/role restructuring (the existing flat task_type + agent_roles.py model already covers this and is explicitly being kept).

Per operator directive: this phase is to be implemented by Fable (opencode_claude) specifically, not left to normal provider rotation.

ADDENDUM 2026-08-02 (Claude Code, folded in rather than opened as a separate phase): live-diagnosed tonight's kai-chat 502 down to root cause -- core.llm_clients._post_json only captured/classified a provider's real error body on HTTP 429, so a 402 (e.g. OpenRouter 'requires more credits') fell through to the generic '{provider} request failed: HTTPError' string, which (a) hid the real, actionable cause (both the shared OPENROUTER_API_KEY and the dedicated DEEPSEEK_OPENROUTER_API_KEY are OpenRouter-credit-exhausted, confirmed live: 'requested up to 65536 tokens, can only afford ~4823') and (b) meant delegate() kept retrying those candidates every call instead of deprioritizing them the way a confirmed quota_exceeded provider already is. Fixed: _post_json now captures/classifies any 4xx/5xx the same way 429 already was (402 treated as quota_exceeded alongside 429; the rest as provider_error), and the real detail rides along in the raised RuntimeError. Full non-external-API suite green (1062 passed) before and after; production memory/*.json diff-checked untouched by the test run per OPERATIONS.md's own deploy checklist. This is a strict subset of item (3)'s scope (provider_health accuracy) -- item (3)'s wall-clock degraded-state detection is still fully open and unaffected by this. Remaining real-world action, not code: Gemini is separately quota 429'd on its own billing, and both OpenRouter keys need credits added at openrouter.ai/settings/credits for 'planning' role fallbacks to actually recover.

OPERATOR OVERRIDE 2026-08-02: give the newly-registered native DeepSeek providers (item 1, DEEPSEEK_NATIVE_PRO_API_KEY / DEEPSEEK_NATIVE_FLASH_API_KEY -- confirmed live again today, both responded correctly) HIGHEST priority in ROLE_PROVIDERS for every text_task role they're eligible for (subject to item (2)'s requires_file_access filtering, which still applies -- these are plain text_task providers, no file/tool access). This explicitly supersedes the general 'new providers slot in after existing top-priority providers' rule from 17M/this phase's own opening -- that rule protected existing providers from being starved by new/free additions; the operator has now directed the opposite for these two specifically. Do not read this as license to reorder any other provider's position -- it applies only to the two native DeepSeek entries.

OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-08-02 (refines item 1's scope -- read this before implementing item 1): core.ai.ai_router.chat() (the function behind POST /kai/chat and the Telegram inbound-reply bridge -- i.e. 'ask Kai what's going on') must be HARDWIRED to deepseek_native_flash specifically, not merely added into the general 'planning' rotation as item 1's original wording implies. Concretely: chat() must call the deepseek_native_flash provider directly (or route through a new, single-candidate task_type/role dedicated to it) with NO fallback to gemini/openrouter/deepseek(openrouter)/claude for this specific caller -- those stay exactly as they are for every other task_type (planning/documentation/review/etc still rotate normally). Rationale, confirmed live tonight: this operator-facing Q&A path 502'd because 3 of its 4 candidates were simultaneously credit/quota-exhausted (OpenRouter 402 on two different keys, Gemini 429) and the 4th (claude/CloudCLI) returned an empty response for this prompt shape. deepseek_native_flash is on its own native api.deepseek.com key, confirmed live twice today (2026-08-02), with no shared-quota exposure to any of those four. Operator wants this specific channel to stop depending on Claude Code -- or on any rotation that could land on a currently-broken candidate -- for 'is Kai actually telling me what's happening' to keep working.

OPERATOR REFINEMENT 2026-08-02 (softens the 'no fallback' wording above -- read this too before implementing): deepseek_native_flash stays PRIMARY and hardwired for both the chat() Q&A path and 17T's digest, but add exactly ONE fallback behind it: 'claude' (via CloudCLI, same as its role everywhere else in the router). Operator's own words: 'if a provider fails and you are available you can take over.' Do NOT re-add gemini/openrouter/deepseek(openrouter) to this role's candidate list -- those are the three that actually caused tonight's failure (two credit-exhausted 402s, one quota 429) and reintroducing them defeats the point of hardwiring this path. phases.name: Parallel build execution + Claude oversight
phases.description: Implements the already-approved design at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-parallel-build-execution-design.md (Status: Approved, not yet implemented) -- follow it directly rather than re-deriving the approach, it has full code sketches for every part below. High-impact, significant improvement to overall throughput: today build_manager.advance_builds() is a plain sequential for loop (confirmed live 2026-07-28) -- one build advances per scheduler cycle regardless of how many are ready, so every other queued roadmap phase waits in a single file behind whichever build is currently running. Four parts: (1) advance_builds() dispatches every ready build (REQUESTED/PLANNING/GENERATING/CODE_REVIEW/DEPLOYING) into a ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_concurrent_builds, default 2 from config/providers.yaml), each worker calling the existing _run_planning/_run_generation/_run_deployment functions unchanged -- single-build behavior stays exactly as today when there's only one ready build; (2) a new core.memory.update(name, mutate_fn) primitive (core/memory.py + core/memory_manager.py), reusing the existing fcntl.flock critical section, so read-modify-write state changes are atomic across threads and processes -- core.ai.ai_router._rotate_candidates (still a non-atomic load-then-save today, confirmed live) is rewritten on top of it, closing the race where two concurrently-dispatched builds could land on the same starting provider; _persist_build() likewise updates one build's record by id instead of resaving the whole list; (3) a new CODE_REVIEW build state between GENERATING and SECURITY_REVIEW -- an automated, purely advisory Claude review of non-Claude-generated builds' diffs (skipped when generated_by == 'claude', since there's no value in Claude reviewing its own work; skipped gracefully if Claude is unavailable) -- never auto-approves or auto-blocks, existing human approval gates are untouched; (4) a GENERATION_DISCIPLINE_PREAMBLE prepended to every generation instruction so every provider is held to the same 'write tests, run them, verify before claiming done' standard this project's own workflow follows.
completion_criteria: advance_builds() runs multiple ready builds concurrently via ThreadPoolExecutor, capped at max_concurrent_builds
Single-ready-build behavior (the common case today) is unchanged -- no regression for sequential operation
core.memory.update() is atomic (fcntl.flock-based) and _rotate_candidates/_persist_build use it, closing the read-then-write race

phases.name: Dual-repo deploy rollback must not discard unrelated uncommitted changes
phases.description: Gap found live 2026-07-29 during manual review of 13Q's deploy (build 18488584), before approving: core.deployment_manager._merge_self_modifying_build's dual-repo rollback path (added by 13Q) reacts to a second-repo (plugin) merge failure by running `git reset --hard <pre_merge_head>` on every already-merged live repo, including SELF_PROJECT_PATH -- this project's own live working directory. Unlike the pre-13Q single-repo failure path (`git merge --abort`, which only undoes the merge attempt itself and leaves any other uncommitted working-tree state untouched), `git reset --hard` unconditionally discards ALL uncommitted changes in the working tree at that moment, not just the merge commit being rolled back. Confirmed live: at the moment of this review, `git status` on SELF_PROJECT_PATH showed an uncommitted roadmap.json change (routine autonomous status-sync churn) -- had a dual-repo deploy been running then and failed on the plugin-repo merge, that uncommitted change would have been silently destroyed as collateral damage of rolling back a merge that had nothing to do with it. Confirmed via tests/test_deployment_manager.py (13Q's own new tests): rollback tests only assert the merge itself is cleanly undone, none set up pre-existing uncommitted changes before triggering the second-repo failure path, so this gap has zero test coverage in either direction. phases.name: Scheduler: periodic systemd watchdog ping during long build cycles
phases.description: Bug, confirmed live 2026-07-28: core/scheduler.py's start() loop only calls notify("WATCHDOG=1") once, after run_cycle() returns -- but run_cycle() -> advance_builds() -> _run_generation() blocks synchronously on a single opencode/claude coding-agent subprocess call that can legitimately run many minutes. When that exceeds the systemd unit's WatchdogSec (currently 600s, set in /etc/systemd/system/ai-orchestrator.service.d/override.conf -- outside this repo, not something this phase touches), systemd SIGABRTs the whole service mid-generation. Observed live: build 13G's first generation attempt was killed this way after ~9 minutes, the service auto-restarted (Restart=always), and the new scheduler cycle immediately re-ran generation on the same still-GENERATING build from scratch (a second opencode run against a workspace that already had partial commits from the killed attempt) -- wasteful and confusing, though not data-corrupting since the workspace is an isolated clone. Fix: ping the watchdog periodically *during* a cycle, not just after it completes, so a long-but-still-alive generation call doesn't look indistinguishable from a hang to systemd. A background thread started at the top of the while loop's iteration (before calling run_cycle()) that calls notify("WATCHDOG=1") on a fixed interval well under WatchdogSec (e.g. every 30-60s), stopped once run_cycle() returns, is the natural fix -- no change to run_cycle()/build_manager/ai_router needed, this is purely scheduler.py's own heartbeat granularity.
completion_criteria: scheduler.py pings WATCHDOG=1 on a fixed interval (well under the systemd unit's WatchdogSec) throughout a cycle's execution, not only once after run_cycle() returns
The periodic ping stops cleanly once the cycle completes or the process is shutting down -- no leaked background thread across loop iterations
No change to run_cycle(), build_manager.py, or ai_router.py -- fix is contained to scheduler.py
New test (or documented manual verification note, if systemd/notify can't be meaningfully unit-tested) covers that the heartbeat mechanism starts and stops correctly around a cycle

Operator directive 2026-08-02: operator asked me (Claude Code) to approve/deploy on their behalf; declined that specifically because it defeats the ARCHITECTURE_APPROVED/DEPLOY_APPROVAL invariant (nothing under core/kai/ calls those functions, by design, enforced by tests/test_kai_identity.py) and reintroduces Claude Code as exactly the single point of failure this whole 2026-08-02 session was about removing. Proposed design (first cut, needs real review before building, which is why this phase is left at status=proposed rather than pending -- it should not enter the queue without an explicit operator decision, unlike the routine wiring work tonight):

(1) SCOPE: architecture-approval gate ONLY, at first. Deploy approval (the step that actually ships code) stays fully manual, no timeout, no exceptions -- revisit only after this is proven out on the lower-stakes gate.
(2) ELIGIBILITY: a build's proposed plan/files_changed must match a narrow, explicit allowlist (starting point: docs-only changes, test-only changes, changes confined to a single app's own project_path under an already-approved template) AND must not touch core/security.py, core/action_policy.py, .env, systemd unit files, docker-compose files, or anything that would expand ALLOWED_ACTIONS. Any file outside the allowlist disqualifies auto-approval for that build entirely -- falls back to fully manual, no timeout, silently (operator sees a normal approval request, not an error).

phases.description:
Foundation for the 'Kai Enterprise Platform' initiative (user proposal 2026-07-29, trimmed after review). Scope, deliberately narrow: local username/password accounts (no external OAuth) plus a capability-based permission check -- capabilities like deploy.build, approve.architecture, chat.use, roadmap.create, provider.configure, each independently checkable in code -- mapped to exactly two initial roles: 'operator' (every capability, i.e. what the single existing bridge-token operator already has today) and 'viewer' (read-only: dashboard/chat reads, no write capabilities). Explicitly deferred from the original proposal, and why: full OAuth (Google/Microsoft/GitHub) + MFA + service accounts was scoped for a system with exactly one real user today -- add a second auth provider only when a real second person needs one, not speculatively. A 6-role taxonomy (Owner/Architect/Developer/Analyst/Customer/Guest) was cut to 2 roles for the same reason -- the capability model means adding a narrower role later is a mapping change, not a redesign, so there is no lock-in cost to starting minimal. The 'Customer' role scoped to assigned projects implied a multi-tenant customer-facing product pivot that was never a stated goal -- if that direction is wanted later it needs its own explicit decision, not a permissions bullet. Multi-organization support (isolated users/projects/learning/providers per org) was cut entirely: there is one organization. None of these are permanently ruled out, just not built until a real need exists -- a future roadmap phase should re-propose them with a concrete driving need, not reintroduce them speculatively.
